overview: The Committee of the Whole conducted its fifth preliminary budget hearing for Fiscal Year 2027, reviewing departmental accomplishments and funding requests for media, health, planning, and executive offices. While most budgets saw routine cost-of-living adjustments, the session was marked by a contentious debate regarding the Law Department’s litigation strategy and lack of transparency.

items.title: Medford Community Media
items.summary: Director Kevin Harrington presented a $276,101.97 budget featuring a new full-time production coordinator and a transition to funding the department through a Special Revenue Fund utilizing PEG fees. The department plans to upgrade chamber and studio equipment and produce outreach videos for city departments.

items.title: Board of Health and Civil Defense
items.summary: Director MaryAnn O'Connor detailed the department's heavy reliance on grant funding for human services and requested that the departments be renamed 'Health and Human Services' and 'Emergency Management' to better reflect their missions. The Council spoke in support of both name changes and reviewed increases for CitizenServe data conversion and a $30,000 rodent control program.

items.title: Planning, Development, Sustainability, and Associated Commissions
items.summary: Director Alicia Hunt outlined progress on the Medford Square transom project and climate resilience initiatives, noting that the climate planner position will transition to full city funding in April 2027. The Council reviewed stipend increases for the Community Development Board and routine budget requests for the Bicycle, Conservation, and Historical commissions.

items.title: Executive, License, and Hormel Commissions
items.summary: Chief of Staff Nina Nazarian presented the executive budget, noting that communication staff funding is shifting to other revenue sources and Zoom and website costs are moving from ARPA to the General Fund. The License Commission budget saw a slight reduction due to the removal of redundant lines, while the Hormel Commission budget remained flat.

items.title: Law Department
items.summary: Councilors proposed cutting $300,000 from the Law Department budget—eliminating the City Solicitor and Professional Services lines—due to frustrations over litigation losses and the administration's failure to provide a requested litigation report. The Chief of Staff argued that these cuts would impair essential legal services and stated that staff cannot fulfill the Council's transparency requests while simultaneously processing a massive public records request.
